description: Knowledge base of common Python / Streamlit bug patterns. Each entry is a retrievable document used by the AI Glitch Investigator's RAG layer.

patterns.name: Streamlit state resets on every rerun
patterns.symptom: A value like a secret number, counter, or score changes or resets every time a button is clicked. State does not persist between interactions.
patterns.cause: Streamlit re-runs the whole script top-to-bottom on every widget interaction. A plain local variable (e.g. secret = random.randint(...)) is recomputed on each rerun instead of being stored in st.session_state.
patterns.fix: Store values that must survive reruns in st.session_state, initializing them only once (if 'secret' not in st.session_state: ...). Read and write st.session_state.secret thereafter.
patterns.keywords: streamlit session_state rerun random randint variable resets every click button secret number changes persist state initialize
patterns.example: secret = random.randint(1, 100)  # BUG: recomputed on every rerun; use st.session_state

patterns.name: Comparing an int against a str
patterns.symptom: Comparisons behave randomly or raise TypeError; hints look correct sometimes and wrong other times, often alternating.
patterns.cause: One operand was cast to a string (e.g. str(secret)) so guess > secret compares int to str. In Python 3 this raises TypeError; a broad except can swallow it and return a garbage result.
patterns.fix: Coerce both operands to int before comparing (guess = int(guess); secret = int(secret)). Remove stray str() casts. Never wrap comparisons in a bare except that hides the TypeError.
patterns.keywords: int str comparison typeerror string cast guess secret compare integer type mismatch even attempt alternating check_guess win too high too low return outcome str secret str str
patterns.example: if guess > str(secret):  # BUG: int vs str; coerce both to int

patterns.name: Backwards / inverted conditional or hint
patterns.symptom: The direction of a hint is reversed: guessing too high says 'go higher', too low says 'go lower'. Logic is inverted.
patterns.cause: The comparison operator points the wrong way, or the hint messages are mapped to the opposite outcome.
patterns.fix: Match each outcome to the correct message: guess > secret means 'too high, go lower'; guess < secret means 'too low, go higher'. Verify the conditional direction against a concrete example.
patterns.keywords: backwards inverted hint higher lower too high too low reversed conditional direction wrong operator mapping
patterns.example: if guess > secret: return 'go HIGHER'  # BUG: too high should say go LOWER

patterns.name: Off-by-one error
patterns.symptom: Attempt counts, 'attempts left', ranges, or loop bounds are off by one. First attempt shows as attempt 2, or one too many/few iterations.
patterns.cause: A counter is initialized at 1 instead of 0 (or vice versa), or a range/limit uses < instead of <= (or an inclusive/exclusive boundary is wrong).
patterns.fix: Start counters at 0 and increment before use, or adjust the boundary comparison. Trace the first and last iteration by hand to confirm the bound.
patterns.keywords: off by one attempts left counter initialize range boundary limit first attempt increment index fencepost
patterns.example: st.session_state.attempts = 1  # BUG: starts at 1, making 'attempts left' off by one

patterns.name: Randomness recomputed / reseeded when it should be stable
patterns.symptom: A random target changes unexpectedly mid-round, or results are non-reproducible when they should be deterministic.
patterns.cause: random.randint / random.choice is called in a code path that runs repeatedly (e.g. every rerun or every submit) instead of once per round; or the value is not stored.
patterns.fix: Generate the random value once per round and persist it (st.session_state or a stored variable). Only reseed on an explicit New Game action.
patterns.keywords: random reseed regenerate every rerun changes mid round persist store once per round new game stable reproducible
patterns.example: secret = random.randint(low, high)  # BUG at top level: regenerates each rerun

patterns.name: Erratic or nonsensical score updates
patterns.symptom: Score jumps around unpredictably, changes on wrong guesses, or randomly adds/subtracts points.
patterns.cause: Scoring logic mutates the score on the wrong outcome (e.g. wrong guesses change score) or introduces randomness/side effects where a deterministic rule is expected.
patterns.fix: Make scoring a pure function of outcome and attempt count. Wrong guesses should not change the score; a win awards points deterministically (e.g. fewer attempts = more points, with a floor).
patterns.keywords: score scoring erratic random points wrong guess subtract add deterministic pure function reward attempts
patterns.example: score += random.choice([-5, 5])  # BUG: wrong guesses should not move score

patterns.name: Mutable default argument
patterns.symptom: A list/dict argument seems to remember values across separate calls; state leaks between invocations.
patterns.cause: A function uses a mutable default like def f(items=[]): the default is created once and shared across all calls.
patterns.fix: Use None as the default and create the container inside the function: def f(items=None): items = items or [].
patterns.keywords: mutable default argument shared list dict persists across calls none sentinel append leak
patterns.example: def add(item, history=[]):  # BUG: history shared across calls

patterns.name: Bare except swallows real errors
patterns.symptom: Code fails silently or returns wrong values with no traceback; bugs are hard to locate.
patterns.cause: A bare 'except:' or 'except Exception: pass' catches and hides the real error (TypeError, ValueError), so a broken code path returns a fallback instead of surfacing.
patterns.fix: Catch only the specific expected exception, keep the block small, and never silently pass. Let unexpected errors propagate or log them.
patterns.keywords: bare except swallow hide error silent pass exception broad catch typeerror fallback traceback

patterns.name: Incomplete state reset (New Game leaves stale state)
patterns.symptom: After a win/loss, starting a new game leaves the board dead: Submit does nothing, old score/status/history persist.
patterns.cause: The reset handler only resets some fields (e.g. the secret) but leaves status, score, or history stale, so guards like 'if status != playing: stop' keep blocking input.
patterns.fix: Reset every piece of state in one place (secret, attempts, score, status, history) and use the current difficulty range. Call it on init and on New Game.
patterns.keywords: incomplete reset new game stale state status score history not cleared submit dead after win loss
patterns.example: st.session_state.secret = randint(...)  # BUG: forgot to reset status/score/history

patterns.name: Hard-coded range / magic number ignores configuration
patterns.symptom: UI text or logic says 'between 1 and 100' even when difficulty or settings imply a different range.
patterns.cause: A range or bound is hard-coded instead of derived from the current difficulty/config, so it desyncs when settings change.
patterns.fix: Derive the range from a single source of truth (e.g. get_range_for_difficulty) and use it for both the secret and the display text.
patterns.keywords: hardcoded range magic number between 1 and 100 difficulty config desync display text single source of truth
patterns.example: st.info('Guess between 1 and 100')  # BUG: hard-coded regardless of difficulty
